question: O polnoci na tradičnej slovenskej svadbe nevesta prichádza o závoj. Čo jej podľa zvyku nasadia namiesto neho?
source_excerpt: married women take down the hair chaplet of the bride and put on a bonnet instead. The bonnet, called čepiec in Slovak, was a symbol of a married woman

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak knows the phrase 'dostať sa pod čepiec', but few connect it to the literal midnight ritual. The player can reason toward the answer from the idiom and gets an 'aha' when the link becomes clear.
extra.verification_notes: Čepčenie replaces the bride's wreath/veil with a married woman's bonnet (čepiec) at midnight; timing varies regionally but the answer is unambiguous (https://spectator.sme.sk/culture-and-lifestyle/c/kidnapping-and-virginity-brace-yourself-for-a-slovak-wedding).

explanation: Čepiec bol znakom vydatej ženy, slobodné dievča ho nenosilo. Odtiaľ pochádza aj obrat, že sa niekto „dostal pod čepiec“.

question: Keď kamaráti počas svadby „unesú“ nevestu, kam ju podľa tradície najčastejšie odvedú?
source_excerpt: when he is finally discovers where his beloved has been kidnapped to, he arrives to buy her back.

extra.why_interesting: Players who have only seen the custom from the wedding hall may not know where the bride actually goes. Most can still work it out from everyday experience. The payoff, that the groom's ransom is the kidnappers' bar bill, makes them smile.
extra.verification_notes: The bride is traditionally 'kidnapped' to a pub and the groom must find her and pay the bill; this is documented mainly for Czech weddings (https://english.radio.cz/node/8044865), and I found no contradicting Slovak source.

explanation: Ženích ju tam musí nájsť a vykúpiť. Výkupné býva často celý účet, ktorý si únoscovia medzitým stihli objednať.
